claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign structure as repetitive, consisting of clearing closed arenas filled with spawning demons before moving through corridors to the next room.

citations.review_text: Great shooter but it gets really repetitive by the end, its the same thing over and over but in different rooms with a different theme. Walk into room, bunch of demons spawn, kill them until the game decides youre done, move on to the next room, repeat until the very end.

The play style is fast, more like old shooters. Gameplay is fun for the first couple of hours but after that it becomes soo repetitive. Glory kills are fun for the first 30-40 times but after playing for 2 hours it stops being interesting. Guns are so similar to each other and doest feel much exciting too. Same monster are spawning in the same spots multiple times for you to kill so you can advance. There is no save system but games own checkpoint which happens before and after fights. Fights got harder with time but the gameplay is still the same. Wouldnt recommend.

Very good arena shooter (8/10)

When a new Doom game was announced to be simply called "Doom", I was not enamoured. This idea of calling sequels/soft reboots by the name of the original game sounded wrong. That's why, when the demo of multi-player launched to a staggering failure, I was happy. "That's what you get for messing with classic games", I thought. Still, I was very happy when the game got positive reviews. In times when First Person Shooters where not what they used to be, it was great to see a classic series return done correctly. So I waited patiently for a better PC to play it. So when I finally got a chance to do so, I enjoyed my time but was quite disappointed at the same time. What matters the most - shooting - was great. Combat felt as it should. But levels left something to be desired. I'm not the biggest fan of arena shooters, those in which levels are built on a pattern of going through a corridor to arrive at the arena where you shoot enemies. And then the next corridor (not literally a corridor, though sometimes yes) leading to the next arena. That's how the game felt. And that's the reason the game got boring at the end for me. As someone who was basically running in circles in every arena, every arena felt the same. So while I was planning on finding all secrets and collecting all that was to be collected, after beating the game, I didn't really feel like it.
Overall, it was fun, maybe not exactly what I would want from an FPS, still, I can appreciate Doom (2016) as it is a very well-done game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game includes a separate third-party launcher featuring advertisements and announcements for other titles.

citations.review_text:
better than Eternal and Dark Ages but rating down because of jank (especially on SteamOS), really long load times, snapmap never works saying I have no storage, typing text in-game doesn't work, never saves my progress or settings the last few times I've tried playing

also all the spam ads on the main menu is annoying, devs stop doing this bs please

Random frame drops, a 3rd party launcher with out-of-date advertisements for worse games, and unskippable cutscenes are what plague this otherwise absolutely mid game. 

Firstly, I get it's from 2016, but you've had a decade and at any random moment I go from 100 fps to 20. Are you too busy being bought out by Microslop to code a game for a game genre where fps are essential? Fps are one of the most important parts of fps games, but you seem to have forgotten that to make all the visuals R E D. 

Also, why do we have a separate DOOM launcher for year-old announcements of even worse games? I don't want to play Dark Ages, and I certainly don't want to pre-order it a year after it's awful release. 

Finally, for a story that establishes "Doomguy doesn't give a heckin f**k about the story!" this game sure seems awfully focused on stopping all your gameplay for a couple minutes to exposit why you're killing demons. DOOM 1993 didn't care about that and it was a good game, so why should DOOM 2016?

Also, game feels very corpo-borpo in a way I can't really describe. Mostly just the plushies breaking what little immersion this game has. With all these frustrations, I think I'll pull an anti-Under-the-Mayo and just play Ultrakill.

single_points.text: One reviewer says switching the graphics API from OpenGL 4.5 to Vulkan resolves severe frame drops.

citation.review_text:
Doom (2016) brings the classic Doom formula into a more modernised Fist-person shooter approach. Gameplay wise it is reminiscent of the older games but improves on them such as weapon mods giving new functions to familiar guns, new animations for killing demons with glory kills and character upgrades. The gunplay is smooth and satisfying. Maps are bigger and contain collectables to upgrade the slayer and his arsenal or to give extra lore for this era of Doom. All the classic demon types throughout the old games appear in the game and has other callbacks such as hidden level sections designed after Doom 1. The story is straightforward featuring another demonic invasion on Mars with the slayer tasked to stop it again but expands more on the worldbuilding than previous Doom games did.

The game features multiplayer (dependent on current active player base but can play with friends) and a level creator where you can design your own Doom levels or play other people's creations.

Performance wise the game runs great but needs some tinkering within the settings as the default options do not give the best performance. The default option for the API is OpenGL 4.5 but with this option I noticed sever frame drops when a lot of enemies are on screen or during certain glory kill animations. Switching to Vulkan fixed all of these issues. The issues for the API could stem that OpenGL 4.5 is meant for older hardware from even before Doom (2016) came out with Vulkan being the better option for setups that can handle or overperform on the game. When switching to Vulkan it will automatically close and reopen the game, however I found that doing this will cause frame drops while pausing the game or using the mini map. This was fixed by manually closing and reopening the game and did not face any more frame drops or stuttering. Regardless whether your setup can output 60 FPS or more, all cinematics/scripted cutscenes will play at a capped 60 FPS and with one section which where you …

If I could have a neutral game review I would rate it neutrally.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Experienced players note that multiplayer modes suffer from low activity while the core combat remains familiar.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the multiplayer mode suffers from low player counts and is difficult to find active matches in naturally.

citations.review_text:
10 years later and I finally decided to fully commit to playing the entire series of the Doom relaunch if you will. I had an absolute blast with this and all three of them as a matter of fact. For a game that's 10 years old it still stands up in every way you could hope for. It's gritty, it's dark, and it's absolutely non-stop fun all coated in a fantastically optimized and gorgeous visual engine. It's very evident from the get go that Bethesda and idS knew what they they wanted to accomplish in bringing this series back to the forefront of gaming and they completely succeeded from top to bottom. It definitely has a couple of technical hiccups depending on what you have under the hood of your PC but after some digging I was able to find that you can minimalize almost all of them by running the game in Vulkan and not DX. 

For achievement hunters/completionists I will say that the multiplayer actually is a blast and would have been fantastic to experience when it was relevant and live but unfortunately it's as dead as it gets and really the only way to complete those MP achievements while retaining your sanity is to boost it and definitely still during off hours so you have less of a chance of being interrupted by the same few people that have been playing it since the beginning and now just enjoy trolling or cheating. You also can't do them in private lobbies which makes it worse. 

All in all I would fully recommend this to just about any type and level of gamer as the difficulty and tuning options really do make it easy for anybody interested and it's a fantastic start to getting into this series especially with Eternal and Dark Ages to follow!

I used to pirate this game because I didn't have any money, but through family sharing I was able to play it and oh boy it is such a blast. So I ended up bought the Doom Anthology bundle and having so much fun!

The only shooters I've ever played were Bioshock 1, Medal of Honor, Resident Evil 4 and Cyberpunk but to me I genuinely like DOOM's gameplay more. It's fast, crisp, tons of enemies and more importantly, bloody and gore. And honestly, the story is not half bad even if it's not the main focus of the game. I believe this game has semented itself to be the start of the modern DOOM games, the likes of DOOM Eternal and DOOM The Dark Ages, and even then this game is still fresh to come back to. Plus there are also some parts of the game that gave me horror vibes which is pretty cool.

Though I have to admit, I haven't tried multiplayer as I heard that it's really quiet, but the main campaign is good enough for me to highly recommend others to play it.

Lowkey my favorite of the modern DOOM games ngl.

multiplayer also rocks, but it's pretty much dead.

Amazing OST too, be a shame if something happened.

100% Achievement Review

I have been playing all the Doom games in order of release, and I gotta say I like the evolution of the series and the leaps this one took.

This seems to be a soft reboot of the series after the events of DOOM 3, as it doesn't seem to have direct tiest to the events a few years earlier, but also seems that it logically COULD be what happened if the UNC when full tilt on the demon worshipping after the events of DOOM 3. The game is still level based, but after DOOM 3 had no map despite all the previous games having the famous automap, this DOOM brought back the map in glorious 3d, and let you unlock upgrades to see all the collectibles (except secret areas). I did need to still follow a guide for secret areas, because while most I could get just by looking at the collectibles, the secret doom level rooms in each level were not marked on the map and had to be sussed out on my own or with a guide.

The story does just sort-of end. You fight the end boss who was the main villainess the whole game, but she was only one cog in the machine and this game was designed to have the story continue in DOOM Eternal, which kept most of the same mechanics introduced in this entry.

The worst part about this 100% was the multiplayer. By far the most annoying in the series, and I've played the multiplayer in all of them. You have to get to a minimum of Eschelon Rank 8. Each 'Eschelon' is 50 levels of multiplayer grinding. I got a boosting group which can net you like 15-20 levels per match (like 30 minutes), but finding a persistant group of a minimum of 4 players to boost it for an 8-10 hour multiplayer grind hoping no randoms join and duck up your groove was a nightmare. The multiplayer is still suprisingly active even after the launch of Doom The Dark Ages (I don't know what the multiplayer sitch is in that one, but I know DOOM Eternal only took like an hour to boost with 2 friends)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign structure as repetitive, relying on a predictable cycle of locked combat arenas where players must defeat waves of spawning enemies to progress.

citations.review_text:
Doom (2016) feels like a hybrid between Doom (1993), Doom II and Doom 3 with some Quake influences thrown in the mix. The combat is intense with emphasis on constant movement, where the mantling ability and double jump boots give additional movement possibilities.

The classic Doom levels are a nice touch akin to classic Wolfenstein 3D levels in the Wolfenstein The New Order and Wolfenstein The Old Blood. The use of frequent holograph sequences is an interesting way of forwarding the story that does not slow game progression too much. I wonder whether the use of holographs was inspired by how the film Prometheus (2012) used them?

The locked combat arenas with enemies repeatedly spawning in, can become tedious, especially when replaying missions to find missed secrets and collectibles and when upgrading runes or mastering weapon modifications. But first time playthrough is amazing and some of the environments feel amazingly large and open. The atmosphere and visual storytelling are top-notch. The soundtrack by Mick Gordon is great as well.

A nervous and rewarding gameplay the game prohibits to stay under cover and pushes to constant aggressiveness. The mechanics of Glory Kills (brutal hand-to-hand executions to recover life) and the chainsaw (to obtain ammunition) create a frantic and fluid action loop. A masterful soundtrack. Composed by Mick Gordon, industrial metal music adapts dynamically to the intensity of the fights, increasing the feeling of power tenfor. An iconic arsenal and bestiary. The return of classic weapons (Super Shotgun, BFG 9000) with alternative shots and improvements offers an excellent feeling. The emblematic demons of the license have various attacks that force you to constantly dodge. An impeccable technical achievement. Powered by the id Tech 6 engine, the title displays detailed graphics and exemplary fluidity at 60 frames per second. An award-winning exploration. The levels are full of secret passages, runic challenges and armor improvements that encourage you to search every corner of the Martian facilities and the Hells. Now The negatives A repetitive campaign structure. The progression is based on a predictable chain of closed arenas where you have to eliminate all the demons to unlock the next door. A very set back scenario. The story only serves as a pretext for the action with unremarkable secondary characters, even if the game plays the card of self-mockery in the face of its own narration. A disappointing multiplayer mode. General and soulless, the multiplayer suffers from a system of predefined classes (loadouts) that betrays the original spirit of the series. A lack of boss fights the low number of clashes against major bosses throughout the adventure. A demanding difficulty curve. Although fair, the game requires quick adaptation and can severely punish players who neglect the search for improvements or who remain static.

Fun for the first few couple hours with solid presentation, a great soundtrack and enjoyable gameplay.

I'd say the game overstays its welcome, the novelty wears out before you reach the mid-point and the repetition kicks in hard. Every 60+ minute long map plays out the exact same way with the colored cards, skulls or whatever else, combat rooms whenever there is an interactable etc. The bosses are very fun but there are fewer than a handful of them and they are crammed into the second half of the campaign. Not sure why there couldn't be a boss for each mission, that alone might've actually turned this into a Recommend for me.

Regardless of what the visual design may imply, the combat doesn't always feel as heavy as it looks. It actually feels a little floaty at times. Particularly, the handgun feels like a peashooter and the shotgun doesn't have as much oomph as I would like - the alternative firing modes do help a little. The other weapons are generally fine though, my favorite is the Gauss Cannon.

As for the story, most people, including superfans of the genre, would tell you that you don't play boomer / arena shooters for the story but I might as well comment on it. There's a barebones story here, some cheesy dialogue and audio logs to go with it. The ending is sequel-bait, I wasn't satisfied with it at all.

Very glitchy and buggy. I was often getting stuck inside enemies because they got close to me while I was mid-glory kill. It happened particularly often with the Caco demons. Other times, glory kills caused me to clip through the environment or fall through the floor, and then off map and into my death. Not a huge deal but it does get progressively more annoying as it keeps happening.

My biggest issue with Doom is how dull it gets outside of short bursts of playing it but I guess that might be an issue with most boomer / arena shooters as these games are simplistic to a fault. That works for a ton of people but it doesn't cut it for me, at least not anym…

Main menu screen is 90% spammed with ads.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Longtime players praise the standout soundtrack while noting that level repetition and dead multiplayer persist.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the level design and enemy types can become repetitive over time.

citations.review_text:
Beating this game on Ultra Violence, the combat loop is VERY VERY good, each enemy poses a unique attack pattern and the heavy enemy spawns keep you constantly on your toes as demon hordes work together to flush you out.

The level design and enemy types can feel a bit repetitive over time unfortunately, but the core gameplay mechanics are so fun that it stays engaging throughout the full game. Doom 2016 captures the magic and brutal spirit of the original games while implementing modern game design advancements.

The gunplay is HIGHLY responsive and glory kills fit into the flow state naturally (they too suffer from being repetitive after a while). You do get hit with overwhelming fights on higher fifficulties but it never feels straight up unfair because you KNOW you can push through it.

The weakest part of the game is easily the bosses..., they aren't bad and they are reasonably well crafted but they feel tedious and slow compared to the relentless pace of the base game or the bosses introduced in Eternal and Dark Ages, instead of swapping weapons strategically for specific enemies like you do in standard arenas the boss fights mostly boil down to dumping every piece of ammo you have in massive bullet sponges.

Now one thing that has to be said: the heavy metal soundtrack is HANDS DOWN the best it has EVER been in any Doom game. Mick Gordon's industrial low tuned metal drives the actual gameplay and it shows, the music kicks in as the combat intensifies, pumping pure adrenaline directly into your veins

The last important thing to mention is the very much appreciated modding community that has developed countless mods to add even more enemies, weapons, skins etc... to the game. I will never thank enough the whole modding community for this game and the other Doom games.


Overall this is exactly what a reboot should be.
Short, sweet and immensely satisfying.
8.5/10 the slayer approves
++++++++++
(Fun fact: I was able to play this on an android.)

Bought this on sale a while back and honestly it is pretty good if you just want to shoot stuff, but people hype it up a bit too much. The graphics hold up well and the gunplay feels heavy, but it gets repetitive faster than I expected.

The main issue is the level design. You literally just walk down a dark hallway, get locked in a room, kill a wave of demons, and then repeat that exact same loop for 8 hours. The story is basically non-existent, taking damage in the middle of all the chaos is hard to track, and there are only like three boss fights in the whole game. The platforming sections also feel totally out of place.

The good part is the actual shooting and the overall vibe. You do not feel like you are trapped in a room with demons, the demons are trapped in a room with you and it is their end. Swapping between weapons feels smooth, glory kills are satisfying, and the soundtrack goes hard. It is a solid action game to blitz through over a weekend, but nothing mind-blowing.

- hearing the main menu music
- hearing the intro narration
- watching the intro
Watching the Title drop sealed the deal.
This game is fkn amazing in every aspect. Don't even get me started on the Soundtrack, you've already listened to it anyway. 
275 hours just replaying the campaign over and over again.
I have absolutely nothing to criticise.
